title: Greek-style coffee shop opens on West Gay Street; 7 Brew drive-thru follows Monday
summary: Brewing Love has opened at 145 W. Gay St., pouring freddos, the iced coffee popular in Greece, along with iced matcha and pastries. Drive-thru chain 7 Brew is set to open at 829 Paoli Pike on Monday, Nov. 16.

title: Museum and heritage center proposed beside Paoli Battlefield goes to Malvern council
summary: Paoli Memorial Grounds will ask Malvern Borough Council on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to approve a museum and heritage center at 404 Monument Ave., next to the Revolutionary War battlefield.

title: SALT supporters launch $2 million drive to buy the theater's building
summary: After West Pikeland supervisors put the municipal building at 1645 Art School Road up for bid, three members of the Chester Springs theater community started a fundraiser so SALT Performing Arts can buy its home before bidding closes in early December. It has passed $60,000, and a donor is matching gifts up to $50,000.

title: Borough seals a time capsule to be opened in 50 years
summary: About 30 residents gathered at the Chester County Welcome Center in the Historic Courthouse to load a capsule with a library card, a Henderson High School yearbook, the borough flag, a Growers Market flyer and a painting of longtime hot dog vendor Scott "Wally" Vassil. Residents and schoolchildren donated the items through the borough's Parks and Recreation Department.
loc: Chester County Welcome Center, Historic Courthouse, West Chester

title: Santa at the Square brings luminaries and food trucks to Marshall Square Park Dec. 5
summary: Downtown West Chester's free holiday evening runs Saturday, Dec. 5, from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. with photos with Santa, live music, children's crafts and hundreds of luminaries lighting the park. Leashed pets are welcome.
loc: Marshall Square Park, 405 N. Franklin St., West Chester

title: Veterans Day parade ends with the courthouse lit green
summary: American Legion Post 134's parade wound through the borough Sunday afternoon and finished with speeches before about 250 people at the Historic Courthouse. Vietnam veteran Jim Oram launched Operation Green Light there, handing out green bulbs for residents to display at home as a sign that veterans are welcome.
loc: Historic Chester County Courthouse, High and Market streets, West Chester

title: Uwchlan supervisors reject 492-home plan for Lionville Station Road farmland
summary: The board voted unanimously Nov. 4 to deny Rockwell Development Group's rezoning request and plan for an age-restricted neighborhood on 237 acres owned by the Downingtown Area School District, citing density, traffic and the cost to taxpayers. Rockwell says it expects to return within 60 days with a plan that fits the current zoning.

title: Downingtown STEM Academy named a Pennsylvania Blue Ribbon School
summary: The state Department of Education picked the academy as one of 12 schools statewide for its 2026 Blue Ribbon list, which weighs academic achievement and improvement, school culture and special education supports. The International Baccalaureate high school opened in 2011 and enrolls about 950 students; Lionville Elementary earned the same honor in the program's first year.

title: Retired Seabee spends his days repairing headstones at Oaklands Cemetery
summary: Ed Dougherty, 65, who served in the Navy from 1979 to 1985, cleans, resets and repairs grave markers at the historic cemetery and replaces tattered flags on veterans' graves, including about 30 in the soldiers' lot. He began walking the grounds to rebuild his strength after a double lung transplant.

title: Library's Holiday Home Tour opens seven decorated houses Dec. 5
summary: The 15th annual self-guided tour runs Saturday, Dec. 5, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., with seven private homes and three other stops dressed for the season. All proceeds go to the West Chester Public Library.
loc: West Chester Public Library, 415 N. Church St., West Chester

title: Hometown Christmas Parade returns Dec. 4 with more marching bands
summary: The Greater West Chester Chamber of Commerce's free parade runs Friday, Dec. 4, rain or shine, starting with the tree lighting at 6:30 p.m. and the procession at 7. This year's lineup adds marching bands by popular demand, works in an America250 tribute and ends with Santa.
